title: argentinian-tomato-lasagna
description: buttery, molten dish featuring tomato and ferment-kimchi in a lacto-vegetarian-friendly argentinian style. perfect for a dinner gathering

ingredients.name: freshly ground beef fat or vegetable oil

instructions: cook the lasagna noodles according to the package instructions and set aside.
in a large saucepan, sauté the onion and garlic until the onion is translucent.
add the ground beef fat or vegetable oil to the saucepan and stir to combine with the onion and garlic.
add the tomato paste to the saucepan and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
add the diced tomatoes to the saucepan and stir to combine with the tomato paste and onion mixture.
bring the sauce to a simmer and let it cook for 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
in a large bowl, combine the cooked lasagna noodles, tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and fresh cilantro.
mix well to combine the ingredients.

in a baking dish, create a layer of the tomato sauce followed by a layer of the noodle mixture. repeat this process until all the ingredients are used up, finishing with a layer of tomato sauce on top.
cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes.
remove the aluminum foil and continue baking for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
remove the lasagna from the oven and let it cool for 10-15 minutes before serving.
serve the argentinian tomato lasagna hot, garnished with additional fresh cilantro if desired.
store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
reheat the lasagna in the oven or microwave before serving.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
